pending.body: The test does not assert DO (dissolved oxygen) or alkalinity per-liter deltas after the tick. Nitrification consumes O2 and alkalinity via fixed stoichiometric factors (o2_for_aob=3.43, o2_for_nob=1.14, etc.), so these are derived from the N deltas. However, a volume-dependent bug in the DO/alkalinity bookkeeping code path (lines 230-235, 288-289, 332-334, 362-364 of nitrogen_cycle.rs) would not be caught. Add assertions for DO and alkalinity per-liter deltas alongside the existing TAN/NO2/NO3/DOC/DON checks to close this gap.

The extreme-scale test (concentration_kinetics_volume_independent_extreme_scales) does not include the Monod factor verification section that the primary test has. While the per-liter delta check is the stronger assertion, the acceptance criteria call for verifying Monod factors specifically. Add the same Monod factor comparison block (or factor it into a shared helper) so both tests cover both criteria.

Preserve explicit zero/custom substrate area multipliers instead of treating them as missing. `SubstrateLayerState::resolved_colonizable_area_factor` in `crates/tank_core/src/types/substrate.rs:44-49` falls back to the kind default whenever the serialized factor is `0.0`, and `refresh_habitat_registry` in `crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:245-248` writes that fallback back into the saved state. Because substrate preset validation explicitly allows non-negative factors (`crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:290-318`), a deliberate `0.0` multiplier cannot survive refresh/load, and `migrate_v6_to_v7` in `crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:632-673` also hard-codes kind defaults instead of preserving custom saved area scaling. Only fall back when the field is absent/non-finite, or derive the migrated factor from the saved `colonizable_area_cm2`.
